answer: Bonded stake with slashing: each agent must lock a deposit before it can vote or earn, so its identity carries a costly signal. If peers prove two identities double-signed or colluded, both bonds are burned. Like guarding copper wire from scrap thieves while ferrous junk lies ignored, it protects what is worth stealing: an attacker running 1,000 sybils must lock 1,000 bonds and loses them all once caught.
